items.body:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-84999 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Pie Register Premium plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unrestricted File Type Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.0 via the piereg_file_upload function. This is due to the plugin performing file type validation via wp_check_filetype and wp_check_filetype_and_ext but never checking whether those validation calls produced errors before move_uploaded_file() is called, combined with no nonce or capability check on the AJAX handler.
items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-84999 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Pie Register Premium plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unrestricted File Type Upload in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.0 via the piereg_file_upload function. This is due to the plugin performing file type validation via wp_check_filetype and wp_check_filetype_and_ext but never checking whether those validation calls produced errors before move_uploaded_file() is called, combined with no nonce or capability check on the AJAX handler. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files of dangerous types (e.g. PHP scripts) that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. The server returns the generated destination filename in the response, giving the attacker the exact path needed to trigger the uploaded file.

Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-106013 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Jupiter X Core plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via the Twitter/X Social Login handler in all versions up to and including 4.61.0. The vulnerability exists within the verify_twitter_callback function because after exchanging the visitor's oauth_verifier for their access token, the handler never calls setOauthToken() to reassign the returned credentials to the TwitterOAuth client, causing the subsequent account/verify_credentials API call to remain signed with the site operator's stored Access Token and Access Token Secret rather than the authenticating visitor's token. This causes the X API to return the profile of the X application owner instead of the signing-in visitor, and the plugin then resolves and authenticates a WordPress account solely by matching that owner's email address via wp_set_auth_cookie(), allowing unauthenticated attackers to gain authenticated access as the WordPress user whose email corresponds to the X app owner, who is typically the site administrator.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-287

Vulnérabilité élevée CVE-2026-33944 affectant dolibarr/dolibarr (composer) (score CVSS 8.8).

Dolibarr has SQL Injection in societe/class/societe.class.php via localtax1_value parameter

An authenticated user with standard "Third Party: Create/Edit" permission can extract any data from the database, including password hashes, API keys, and all business data.

Tested on Dolibarr v23.0.0 (latest stable), default installation via official Docker image, MariaDB 10.11. No custom modules, no modified configuration.

Vulnerable code ( societe/class/societe.class.php , line 1672):

The alpha input filter strips HTML tags and double quotes but does not strip single quotes, parentheses, commas, or SQL keywords. Since the injection point is in a numeric SQL context (no quotes around the value), the attacker needs none of the filtered characters.

Why the WAF does not block this: Dolibarr's WAF ( waf.inc.php ) only checks SQL injection patterns in GET parameters, not POST. The POST-based lt1 parameter bypasses it entirely.

The same vulnerability exists for localtax2_value (parameter lt2 ) at line 1682.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par CyberScoop.

The Office of the National Cyber Director has rolled out its second regional cyber pilot program, this one focused on rural hospitals. National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross visited South Carolina on Monday to debut the six-month program, Project Lifeline 250, which connects industry with rural hospitals. The concept is similar to the first pilot program in Texas that connected industry with the water sector . “Project Lifeline 250 connects the world-leading American industry with rural hospitals and uses the greatest American tools and capabilities to defend hospital networks; deploy physical back up devices after an initial incident to ensure an impacted hospital can still provide critical care; and identify high-risk and legacy devices and replace them,” Cairncross said in a statement. Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services says British police data has been breach several times this decade through third-party IT suppliers.

Hackers have repeatedly compromised third-party suppliers holding British police data since 2021, according to a report published Tuesday by His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services.

The inspectorate, which oversees policing in England and Wales and fire services in England, said the Police Digital Service and the National Police Chiefs’ Council shared “information on multiple cyberattacks” affecting “third-party ICT supply chains which held police information.”

The report does not say how many attacks took place, which suppliers or forces were affected, or whether data was stolen in these supply-chain incidents. The inspectorate said it purposefully removed operational details that it considered unsuitable for the public domain.

Neither the Home Office, Britain’s interior ministry, nor the National Police Chiefs’ Council responded to questions about whether police data was compromised in the supplier attacks.

The watchdog said the Police Digital Service recorded 252 cybersecurity incidents affecting policing in the first three months of this year, as well as 796 “near misses,” which the report defined as incidents with no harmful breach of data or IT systems.

The report does not say how many of the 252 incidents involved data loss, nor does it break the figure down beyond saying the incidents included malware attacks, unauthorized access attempts and accidental disclosures by police staff.

Incident de sécurité rapporté par The Record.

Cybercriminals are stuffing infostealer malware into bogus apps aimed at tracking gas prices, police activity, drone strikes and other information of concern to average Russians, researchers said.

Cybercriminals are exploiting fuel shortages and fears of drone attacks in Russia to trick users into downloading malicious Android apps designed to steal personal and financial information, according to a new report.

The latest campaign targets Russian drivers with an app that claims to show the locations of traffic police patrols, speed cameras and gas stations with fuel in stock. Instead, it delivers ZloyRAT, an Android trojan capable of collecting sensitive information and accessing functions on infected phones, according to researchers at Russian cybersecurity firm F6.

The malware is also being distributed through two other fake applications: GosuVPN, advertised as a free government-backed service for accessing the unrestricted internet, and Drone Radar, which claims to display drone attacks on an interactive map in real time.

All three apps are promoted through a website registered in early October, researchers said, adding that they had requested to block the website in Russia.

The campaign comes as Russia faces widespread fuel shortages and rising gasoline prices, driven in part by repeated long-range Ukrainian drone and missile strikes on Russian oil refineries. The threat actor behind the campaign also remains unknown

F6 said malicious applications targeting drivers are typically advertised in online communities for truck drivers, taxi operators and delivery workers.

items.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
items.body:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Schneier on Sec..

Interesting research: “ AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities ” Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited.
items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Schneier on Sec..

Interesting research: “ AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities ” Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a small chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

DOJ action against five foreign nationals — plus a sting in Madagascar — highlight the expanding global reach of the scam center industry.

The Justice Department said it disrupted a Madagascar-based scam operation that allegedly stole hundreds of thousands from Americans through fictitious NFT investment schemes.

The indictment said Wa worked with accomplices in China in coordinating and funding the scheme, which allegedly moved to Madagascar last year after law enforcement takedowns in Cambodia.

An FBI unit went to Madagascar in August and gained access to more than 3,000 devices, prosecutors said. The sting revealed the detailed inner-workings of the operation and provided concrete links between incident reports filed by victims in the U.S. and scammers conducting the scheme from compounds in the country’s capital, Antananarivo.

The Justice Department noted that during the trip, its officers went to 13 scam compounds with the Madagascar National Police (MNP) but were “stymied” when they tried to interview suspects.

“Madagascar repatriated to China numerous suspects before the investigation was complete,” the Justice Department said. Signal de veille — Infosecurity Mag.

UK police forces and fire and rescue services have been urged to strengthen cybersecurity as rising cyber threats outpace current defenses

The cyber threat to UK police forces and fire and rescue services is growing rapidly and demands a more urgent response, an independent assessment has warned.

The Cybersecurity in Police Forces and Fire and Rescue Services report from His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services (HMICFRS) was published on October 27.

It was compiled from a three-phase inspection carried out between January and May 2026, and involved dozens of interviews, “reality testing,” and scrutiny of over 260 police service and fire and rescue service documents.

“While there have been gradual improvements, many forces and services still need to urgently redouble their efforts to respond to the increased risk of cyber-attacks,” warned Michelle Skeer, His Majesty’s inspector of constabulary.

“Cybersecurity should be viewed as a core organizational priority and not solely a technical risk. Leaders need to prioritize and invest in their cybersecurity arrangements to improve their organization’s ability to prevent, detect, respond to and recover from attacks.”

Signal de veille — Infosecurity Mag.

ISC2’s new Cyber-AI Workforce Coalition serves as a “vendor-neutral convener” to map the future of AI security careers, ISC2 CEO Scott Beale told Infosecurity

After years of tracking the global cybersecurity skills gap through its annual Cybersecurity Workforce Study , ISC2 is taking a more active role in shaping the future of the profession with the launch of its Cyber-AI Workforce Coalition.

Announced on October 20, the new coalition is one of the first major developments introduced by Scott Beale, ISC2’s CEO, who took on the role in December 2025.

Speaking to Infosecurity during the ISC2 Security Congress 2026, in Denver, Colorado, on October 26, Beale said he spent his first six months as CEO listening to the organization’s members.

A key finding from the consultation was that a majority of ISC2 members want the nonprofit to more ambitiously and vocally step into the AI safety and security space.

“We want to be the association that can help prepare the cybersecurity workforce for the many challenges of this AI era,” Beale added.

Beale described the coalition as a “vendor-neutral convener” for global cybersecurity professionals. It aims to include thought leaders like HR managers and CISOs, some of the largest employers of cybersecurity practitioners, standard-setting bodies and even government representatives to discuss how cybersecurity roles are changing because of AI.

Signal de veille — Infosecurity Mag.

ISC2 is seeking 3000 volunteers to enrol to a pilot exam phase for its upcoming AI security certification

Cybersecurity professionals will be able to take the first ISC2-approved AI security exam in early 2027.

The cyber nonprofit behind the Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) qualification announced its 10 th certification during its Security Congress 2026, in Denver, Colorado, on October 26.

This new credential will be dedicated to cybersecurity and AI professionals who want to showcase their knowledge in secure AI-enabled environments.

Speaking to Infosecurity , Scott Beale, CEO of ISC2, said that the certification is still under development and “doesn’t even have a name yet.”

However, he confirmed it is “being built by cybersecurity professionals, for cybersecurity professionals.”

He said the decision to develop a new “AI security benchmark for the cybersecurity industry” partly came from the desire from ISC2 members for the nonprofit to “ambitiously and vocally step into the AI safety and security space.”
